subject: Civil Engineering
title: Pavement Distress: Cracks and Potholes
description: Learn Pavement Distress: Cracks and Potholes in one minute.

hook.text: A pothole swallows your tire. That hole started as a tiny crack months ago.

buildup.text: Fatigue cracking starts from repeated truck loads — alligator-pattern cracks spread.

discovery.text: Water enters cracks, freezes, expands, and pops out chunks — a pothole is born.

twist.text: Rutting happens when asphalt deforms under heavy loads in hot weather — permanent grooves.

climax.text: Pavement management systems track every crack and schedule repairs before potholes form.

punchline.text: Fix the crack and you prevent the pothole. Ignore it and you rebuild.

quiz.question: How does water contribute to pothole formation?
options: Water dissolves the asphalt binder chemically
Water enters cracks, freezes and expands, breaking apart the pavement
Water lubricates the road surface causing tires to erode it faster
